task_criteria: PROOF: `PATH=$PWD/.venv/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH python3 -m pytest tests/test_xml_specs.py::test_selection_skips_a_malformed_unrelated_document -q` prints `1 passed`. FAILIF: any other pass count, a failure, or a collection error.

PROOF: `PATH=$PWD/.venv/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH python3 -m pytest tests/test_xml_specs.py::test_corpus_wide_verbs_still_refuse_a_malformed_document -q` prints `1 passed`. FAILIF: any other pass count, a failure, or a collection error.
PROOF: `grep -c "skipped 1 unreadable document(s)" tests/test_xml_specs.py` prints 2. FAILIF: 0 or 1 - the reported-skip assertion left the suite.
PROOF: `grep -c "Corpus-wide vs selection-scoped" docs/VERBS.md` prints 1. FAILIF: 0 — the selection-scoped vs corpus-wide rule is undocumented again.
PROOF: `grep -c documents_unreadable auger.py` prints 2. FAILIF: 0 - the product stopped emitting the measured corpus counter.
PROOF: `grep -c "tests/test_xml_specs.py" tests/gate.sh` prints 2. FAILIF: 0 or 1 — the pinning suite dropped out of the gate pytest arm.
PROOF: bash -c "git merge-base --is-ancestor dd9e4aee668a071de7eb48374111f179d5a621e2 HEAD; echo rc=$?" prints rc=0. FAILIF: any nonzero rc — the cited fix commit is absent from the graded history.

items.criterion: PROOF: `PATH=$PWD/.venv/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH python3 -m pytest tests/test_xml_specs.py::test_selection_skips_a_malformed_unrelated_document -q` prints `1 passed`. FAILIF: any other pass count, a failure, or a collection error.
items.detail: Ran the exact command: exit_code 0, output `. [100%]` then `1 passed in 0.03s`. The test (tests/test_xml_specs.py:1090) is substantive, not tautological: it builds a 3-document corpus with one MALFORMED file, asserts `list --id W-REQ-1` exits 0 with only the W-REQ-1 row on stdout, asserts `skipped 1 unreadable document(s)` and `zz-broken.xml` on stderr, and asserts the assemble JSON `corpus` dict equals {documents_discovered:3, documents_parsed:2, documents_unreadable:1, documents_selected:1}.

items.criterion: PROOF: `PATH=$PWD/.venv/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH python3 -m pytest tests/test_xml_specs.py::test_corpus_wide_verbs_still_refuse_a_malformed_document -q` prints `1 passed`. FAILIF: any other pass count, a failure, or a collection error.
items.detail: Ran the exact command: exit_code 0, output `. [100%]` then `1 passed in 0.15s`. The test asserts the PAIR on one corpus: `list` exits 0 naming zz-broken.xml, while `validate` and `check` each exit 2 with empty stdout and `spec error (invalid-xml)` naming zz-broken.xml; it additionally asserts unsupported-schema-version and external-entity-forbidden are refused by the selection verbs too.

items.criterion: PROOF: `grep -c "skipped 1 unreadable document(s)" tests/test_xml_specs.py` prints 2. FAILIF: 0 or 1 - the reported-skip assertion left the suite.
items.detail: `grep -c` printed `2`. The two hits are tests/test_xml_specs.py:1116 (the AUG-146 selection test) and tests/test_xml_specs.py:1362 (the AUG-148 symlink test, which also asserts the skip is counted).

items.criterion: PROOF: `grep -c "Corpus-wide vs selection-scoped" docs/VERBS.md` prints 1. FAILIF: 0 — the selection-scoped vs corpus-wide rule is undocumented again.
items.detail: `grep -c` printed `1`. The section at docs/VERBS.md:692-703 states that `validate`/`check`/`bundle` are corpus-wide verdicts that refuse the whole run naming the file (`invalid-xml`, exit 2), that `list`/`assemble` are selection-scoped and skip-and-count to stderr, that `assemble --format json` carries the four `corpus.*` counters, and that the tolerance is exactly one code wide.

items.criterion: PROOF: `grep -c documents_unreadable auger.py` prints 2. FAILIF: 0 - the product stopped emitting the measured corpus counter.
items.detail: `grep -c` printed `2`: auger.py:9042 (docstring) and auger.py:12656, where `_spec_corpus_counts` returns `"documents_unreadable": len(unreadable)`. Verified live rather than by grep alone: `spec assemble --id W-REQ-1 --format json` on a corpus with one malformed file printed `{'documents_discovered': 2, 'documents_parsed': 1, 'documents_selected': 1, 'documents_unreadable': 1}`.

items.criterion: PROOF: `grep -c "tests/test_xml_specs.py" tests/gate.sh` prints 2. FAILIF: 0 or 1 — the pinning suite dropped out of the gate pytest arm.
items.detail: `grep -c` printed `2`: tests/gate.sh:157 (the comment explaining why the suite is named) and tests/gate.sh:206, the actual `python3 -m pytest ... tests/test_xml_specs.py ...` invocation inside `run_pytest_arm`. The suite is genuinely in the executed arm, not only in a comment.

items.criterion: PROOF: bash -c "git merge-base --is-ancestor dd9e4aee668a071de7eb48374111f179d5a621e2 HEAD; echo rc=$?" prints rc=0. FAILIF: any nonzero rc — the cited fix commit is absent from the graded history.
items.detail: Ran the exact command: output `rc=0`, so dd9e4aee is an ancestor of HEAD (4b5c3f3).

items.criterion: The tolerance flag must be reachable from the CLI entrypoint for `list`/`assemble` (selection-scoped) and must NOT be passed by `validate`/`check`/`bundle` (corpus-wide), so the skip is real end-to-end and not only in a test helper.
items.detail: auger.py:12711 `selection_scoped = command in ("list", "assemble")`; auger.py:12725-12727 calls `load_spec_corpus_indexed(a.root, tolerate_unreadable=True, skipped=unreadable)`; the else branch at auger.py:12734 calls the strict `load_spec_corpus(a.root)`. Verified end-to-end on a hand-built corpus with one malformed file: `spec list --id W-REQ-1` -> rc=0, stderr `spec: skipped 1 unreadable document(s) — this verb is selection-scoped`, stdout the W-REQ-1 row; `spec validate` -> rc=2 `spec error (invalid-xml): zz-broken.xml`; `spec check` -> rc=2; `spec bundle W-REQ-1` -> rc=2 (bundle routes through `_xml_spec_documents` at auger.py:13061, which has no tolerance parameter).

items.criterion: The tolerance is one code wide: only `invalid-xml` is skipped; other read-time refusals (unsupported schema version, DOCTYPE/ENTITY, wrong namespace/root) still refuse on the selection-scoped verbs too.
items.detail: auger.py:7883 `SPEC_TOLERATED_UNREADABLE = ("invalid-xml",)` and auger.py:8053 `if not (tolerate_unreadable and exc.code in SPEC_TOLERATED_UNREADABLE): raise`. Verified live: a corpus with a valid a.xml plus a DOCTYPE/ENTITY sibling, `spec list --id W-REQ-1` -> rc=2 `spec error (external-entity-forbidden): zz-doctype.xml` — refused, not skipped. The suite also asserts unsupported-schema-version and external-entity-forbidden refuse on the selection verbs.

items.criterion: The strict default is preserved for existing Python callers: `load_spec_corpus(root)` with no flag still raises the typed SpecError on a malformed document (back-compat of the public loader).
items.detail: auger.py:8706-8707 `def load_spec_corpus(spec_root, *, tolerate_unreadable: bool = False, skipped: list | None = None)` — default False. Verified live: `auger.load_spec_corpus('/tmp/aug146probe/corpus')` on the corpus containing zz-broken.xml raised `SpecError` with code `invalid-xml`. The test also asserts `pytest.raises(auger.SpecError)` with `code == "invalid-xml"` on the same corpus, so the tolerance is opt-in rather than inherited.

items.criterion: A corpus in which EVERY document is unreadable does not silently answer "no-match": the loader raises the real typed error instead of returning an empty index.
items.detail: auger.py:8755-8759 (mirrored at 8830-8833 in `load_spec_corpus_indexed`): `if not documents: first = unreadable[0]; raise SpecError(first["code"], first["detail"])`. Verified live: a corpus containing only only-broken.xml, `spec list --id W-REQ-1` -> rc=2 `spec error (invalid-xml): only-broken.xml: unclosed token: line 2, column 6`, not a silent empty selection.

items.criterion: The tolerance is one code wide: only `invalid-xml` is skipped; other read-time refusals (unsupported schema version, DOCTYPE/ENTITY, wrong namespace/root) still refuse on the selection-scoped verbs too.
items.detail: auger.py:7883 `SPEC_TOLERATED_UNREADABLE = ("invalid-xml",)` and auger.py:8053 `if not (tolerate_unreadable and exc.code in SPEC_TOLERATED_UNREADABLE): raise`. Verified live: a corpus with a valid a.xml plus a DOCTYPE/ENTITY sibling, `spec list --id W-REQ-1` -> rc=2 `spec error (external-entity-forbidden): zz-doctype.xml` — refused, not skipped. The suite also asserts unsupported-schema-version and external-entity-forbidden refuse on the selection verbs.

items.criterion: The strict default is preserved for existing Python callers: `load_spec_corpus(root)` with no flag still raises the typed SpecError on a malformed document (back-compat of the public loader).
items.detail: auger.py:8706-8707 `def load_spec_corpus(spec_root, *, tolerate_unreadable: bool = False, skipped: list | None = None)` — default False. Verified live: `auger.load_spec_corpus('/tmp/aug146probe/corpus')` on the corpus containing zz-broken.xml raised `SpecError` with code `invalid-xml`. The test also asserts `pytest.raises(auger.SpecError)` with `code == "invalid-xml"` on the same corpus, so the tolerance is opt-in rather than inherited.

items.criterion: A corpus in which EVERY document is unreadable does not silently answer "no-match": the loader raises the real typed error instead of returning an empty index.
items.detail: auger.py:8755-8759 (mirrored at 8830-8833 in `load_spec_corpus_indexed`): `if not documents: first = unreadable[0]; raise SpecError(first["code"], first["detail"])`. Verified live: a corpus containing only only-broken.xml, `spec list --id W-REQ-1` -> rc=2 `spec error (invalid-xml): only-broken.xml: unclosed token: line 2, column 6`, not a silent empty selection.
